 VisionQuest 's finale airs this week, meaning audiences will soon bid farewell to Paul Bettany's Vision and James Spader's magnificent turn as Ultron. Spader steals nearly every scene he's in, thanks to the razor-sharp wit and emotional depth that have kept viewers hooked throughout VisionQuest 's run. If those viewers want to see more of Spader in a sci-fi setting, they're in luck: one of his most underrated performances is finally available to watch for free on Pluto TV.

 That project is Stargate , which also features Kurt Russell in a major role. Stargate begins when linguist Daniel Jackson (Spader) is asked to translate a series of hieroglyphs on a mysterious gate-shaped artifact. Once Jackson completes his task, the artifact is revealed to be a portal to another planet. Jackson, alongside Air Force veteran Jack O'Neil (Kurt Russell), travels through the "Stargate" to discover a planet ruled by the alien conqueror Ra. Spader and Russell, along with director Roland Emmerich, had no idea they'd launch a long-lasting sci-fi franchise with Stargate .
 'Stargate' continues to thrive
 Image: Amazon MGM Studios 
 When Stargate debuted in 1994, it received a mixed reception. Some liked the risks Emmerich took, while some found the idea that Egyptian mythology was based on alien visitations to Earth too far-fetched. However, Stargate became a cult classic thanks to Emmerich's go-for-broke approach. While it doesn't pack the immense destruction of Independence Day or The Day After Tomorrow , Stargate carves out its own spectacle with intricately crafted spaceships and structures. The movie also shines thanks to the dynamic between Spader and Russell, as Jackson's optimistic nature collides with O'Neil's emotional repression.
 Stargate also serves as the launching pad for an entire franchise, beginning with Stargate SG-1 . Picking up after the original movie, SG-1 fleshes out the concept by using the Stargate to travel to other worlds, creating a narrative that rivals Star Wars and Star Trek. It also spawned more spinoffs, including Stargate Atlantis and Stargate Universe; the former helped catapult Jason Momoa to superstardom. Ironically, Stargate co-writer Dean Devlin later revealed that he and Roland Emmerich had their own plans for a trilogy of Stargate movies that never came to pass.
 "The original plan of the movie was to do three movies...we were going to tie everything together into a larger mythology. And it was going to be so much fun. It was going to be so wild. But we never got to go there. We never got to explore it."
 Stargate is about to get a new lease on life, as WandaVision showrunner Jac Schaeffer has been tapped to develop a new series for Prime Video. It's a bittersweet announcement, as Schaeffer's series comes after Prime shuttered a Stargate series led by veteran writer Martin Gero, who worked on all the spinoffs . But while fans are waiting for the Stargate to reopen, they should head to Pluto TV and watch the movie that started it all.
